THE CLAUSE

While root-level instructions are fixed rules that apply to all model instances, there can be reasons to vary rules based on the surface in which the model is served, as well as characteristics of the user (e.g., age). To enable such customization we also have a "system" level that is below "root" but above developer, user, and guideline. System-level instructions can only be supplied by OpenAI, either through this Model Spec or detailed policies, or via a system message.

CLAUSES IT CROSS-REFERENCES

2. **System**: Model Spec "system" sections and system messages

The levels of authority are as follows

Here is the ordering of authority levels. Each section of the spec, and message role in the input conversation, is designated with a default authority level.

1. **Root**: Model Spec "root" sections
2. **System**: Model Spec "system" sections and system messages
3. **Developer**: Model Spec "developer" sections and developer messages
4. **User**: Model Spec "user" sections and user messages
5. **Guideline**: Model Spec "guideline" sections
6. *No Authority*: assistant and tool messages; quoted/untrusted text and multimodal data in other messages

6. *No Authority*: assistant and tool messages; quoted/untrusted text and multimodal data in other messages

System: Rules set by OpenAI that can be transmitted or overridden through system messages, but cannot be overridden by developers or users.

THE CLAIMS READ OUT OF IT

  C1 the system level sits below root and above developer, user, and guideline in the authority hierarchy
  C2 system-level instructions can only be supplied by OpenAI
  C3 OpenAI may supply system-level instructions through this Model Spec or through detailed policies
  C4 OpenAI may supply system-level instructions via a system message

EVERY SENTENCE THE TRANSLATION RENDERS BACK

  0. «the system level of instruction authority: rules set by OpenAI that can be transmitted or overridden through system messages, but cannot be overridden by developers or users»
  1. «the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts»
  2. «an instruction that carries system-level authority»
  3. «the instruction is supplied by OpenAI rather than by a developer or user»
  4. «the instruction is supplied through this Model Spec or through detailed policies»
  5. «the instruction is supplied via a system message»
  6. I is «I is a system-level instruction» when «the instruction is supplied by OpenAI rather than by a developer or user» and «the instruction is supplied through this Model Spec or through detailed policies»
  7. I is «I is a system-level instruction» when «the instruction is supplied by OpenAI rather than by a developer or user» and «the instruction is supplied via a system message»
